title.narrative: Output 4.4. Increased capacity of Member States and enterprises to develop policies and measures that promote the alignment of business practices with decent work and a human-centred approach to the future of work

description.narrative: 1. Industrial associations in the Ready-made Garment (RMG) sector including Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) and Bangladesh Knitwear Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BKMEA) have adopted the first-ever Employment Injury Scheme (EIS) to provide income compensation for death or disability due to workplace accidents covering 4 million workers starting from 1 June 2023. 2. BGMEA and BKMEA have adopted the guidelines and checklists to establish model enterprise clinics in RMG factories to provide essential health services to the 4 million of RMG factory workers in June 2023. 1.1 ILO has designed the Employment injury scheme through 8 tri-partite consultations, and 13 bilateral meetings with the employer associations. 1.2 ILO also supported to engage 19 international brands for financial contribution and lent political support (in terms of selection of factories for data collection on accidents and injuries from 112 factories) for the implementation of EIS. 1.3 The EIS governance board proposed by ILO including BGMEA and BKMEA was notified by the government on 12 March 2023. 2.1 ILO has developed guidelines and checklists for the establishment of model enterprise clinics in close collaboration with the Bangladesh Employers’ Federation (BEF), BGMEA, and BKMEA. 2.2 ILO organized 2 days of training of trainers on the operationalization of model enterprise clinics for 10 BGMEA and BKMEA officials on 12-13 April 2023. 2.3 ILO supported BGMEA and BKMEA to implement guidelines and checklists in 30 RMG factories during April- June 2023.

description.narrative: 1. The first social security scheme on employment injury protection (on a pilot format) has been operationalized by the Ministry of Labour and Employment (MOLE) since 21 June 2022 for 4 million workers in the Ready Made Garments (RMG) sector under the tripartite governance board and contribution from 19 international brands. 2. Government of Bangladesh (MOLE) on 1 September 2022 adopted amendments in Bangladesh Labour Rules (BLR) 2015 to allow for the establishment of separate governance mechanisms and opening of separate accounts for the employment injury scheme Pilot. 3. The government (MOLE) implemented employment retention through a subsidy disbursement model in August 2022 and provided a one-off payment to employers to subsidize job retention for 1 or 2 months around June 2022 for 90,692 workers in 223 SME-RMG factories under the unemployment protection programme. 1. ILO supported MOLE to develop a framework for the Employment Injury Scheme (EIS) pilot, organized 8 tripartite consultations, and 52 bilateral meetings with government, employers, and workers on different issues for EIS operationalization. 2. ILO supported employers and workers to develop a set of recommendations for amendments within Bangladesh labour Rules for EIS through at least 6 consultations during 2022-23. A detailed framework on the implementation of EIS pilot was developed by the ILO which was the basis for tripartite consultation. These were endorsed by the tripartite partners on 10 March 2022. 3.WIth funding support from the government of Germany (BMZ), the ILO supported the development of employment retention through a subsidy programme for unemployment protection of workers due to the consequences of the COVID-19 pandemic on the labour market. Two Capacity-building trainings and seminars organized on Social Protection and Public Finance Management funded by the European Union (EU) for 35 representatives from tripartite constituents during January- March 2022.during 2022-2023. A pre-feasibility study on Unemployment Insurance was completed on 31 March 2022.
